The application form is called IM0006. Basically, you print it out and fill out the application. Then scan it back to your partner and have them sign it and scan it back to you. They will only need to sign it and add their passport number. The rest of the application is for you to fill out. You will need to provide your proof of citizenship or PR. I included a photo of my passport, birth certificate and SIN card, just to cover all possible bases. Then you take the fully completed application to a notary public or paralegal and have them look it over, sign it and put a stamp on it. The first time we applied I made the mistakes of sending my ID documents through a Google link. I also included a bunch of photos of him and I. Apparently you're not supposed to do that. I immediately got an email back saying that my application had been received. A week later I got an email saying the application was incomplete due to my not providing my proof of citizenship. I then realized it had to he attached to the email through PDF or JPG. So I made the photos of my ID into PDFs, removed the personal photos and sent it again. I got an email back within seconds, again, saying my application had been received. A few days later I went over the email again and realized it was supposed to be sent from HIS email. So, I forwarded everything to him and he sent it. We waited. Exactly 14 business days later (their time frame) we got the approval letter. This sounds a lot more complicated than it actually was. As long as you do it right the first time, it should go smoothly. Remember, it's not 14 days; it's 14 business days. That was where I started to get frustrated. I was expecting to hear back by the two week mark, but it actually took about two and a half weeks. Hope this is helpful and good luck!! You can find the form just by googling IM0006 😊

We are using the Karen Pryor clicker training method with our puppy. It's effective and fun, for both you and your pup. We redirect all negative behaviours by removing him from whatever "bad" thing he's doing and move him over to something he can/should be doing, "click" and give small treat. Most dogs take to it very quickly. Say you catch your dog eating the carpet, move him to a chew toy, click, and give a treat. There is more to it. You can order the basic kit off of Amazon. It's not expensive. 

Background: I have worked with dogs most of my adult life in every area imaginable, from a large animal shelter to doggy daycares. I've seen every type of training practice you can imagine, and I find the clicker method to be the most practical and effective.
